brief: TS Lombard argues USD/JPY's two-year disconnect from collapsing US-Japan yield spreads is starting to break, as faster BoJ tightening, political tolerance for a stronger yen, and a reversal of Japanese capital outflows align. Intervention started the move, but TS Lombard says repatriation is what sustains it: Japanese investors kept buying foreign assets despite rising domestic yields for two years, and that behavior is now reversing. GPIF's domestic-bond allocation has already risen to 27% from its 25% benchmark, with room to move 6ppt above benchmark, a shift the piece says could remove a major source of foreign-debt demand and add upward pressure on US and European yields as global issuance accelerates. TS Lombard expects quarterly BoJ hikes from January 2027 to a 2% terminal rate by Q4 2027, on negative real rates and a wage-and-services inflation spiral, and sees USD/JPY breaking 150 toward a 130-140 fair value. Speculative positioning remains short, leaving room for forced covering, and a disorderly break could force carry-trade deleveraging across risk assets, for which the piece flags long equity volatility as a hedge.
